- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently dipped.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast peaks at 1.5x recent high or 1.2x 14-day moving average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >1.2x recent 30-day average, reduce by 10-20% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment lag” correction: reduce forecast by 5-15% if sentiment drops below 0.33 within 7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extreme outliers (>±20% from 14-day moving average) unless sentiment strongly supports; use sentiment as a filter for outlier rejection.
